intro: Look up at the rock ridge rising over Lake Van. This is Tushpa, also known as Van Fortress, in Van province, and its story begins in the 9th century BC. Here stood the Urartian capital.
history: Tushpa was founded by King Sarduri, and it became the administrative heart of Urartu. Its royal tombs, cut into the rock, survive to this day, together with its cuneiform inscriptions.
structure-2: You are now at the Sardur Bastion, a defensive bastion built by the Urartian king Sarduri. Pause for a moment and imagine the guards who once kept watch from here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the royal tombs and the cuneiform inscriptions, and look down too, towards old Van city.
facts: Did you know? A trilingual inscription of the Persian king Xerxes is carved into the cliff here. This was the capital of Urartu, and the rock-cut royal tombs and the annals of Argishti I look out from the sheer face of the citadel. Xerxes' trilingual cuneiform inscription is cut into an all but unreachable spot on the cliff, yet it can still be read. And the flat ground below the citadel is where the old city of Van stood before 1915; nothing of it remains now but two mosques.
outro: This brings our journey through Tushpa, Van Fortress, to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This rock has guarded its kings' words for centuries; let it keep them for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
